description.describe_ch:
This course is designed to help students compose great essays. By focusing on various styles of writing, we offer a wide range of support to improve your skills in a multitude of genres, including discursive, analytical, and narrative works, which are essential to all academics and professionals. 

Through the proper use of these skills, students will be able to organize and write very cohesively, paying particular attention to the following five criteria:  thesis/focus, organization, content/development, syntax/diction, and mechanics/grammar.  

Throughout the course, students must write at least three essays, each of which the instructor shall grade with both written comments and verbal feedback.

The design of this course shall enhance your writing capability to a standard that should match all college students at home and abroad. The core skills gained herein will solidify your future progress both in academia and in other professions.

gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol_en:
Guidelines for the Academic Use of AI Tools
01
Under the guidance of the course instructor and in accordance with standards of academic integrity, students are expected to use AI tools responsibly to enhance learning efficiency and effectiveness and to accomplish course objectives at each stage of study.
02
Students should develop a clear understanding of the strengths, limitations, and potential implications of AI tools. While information technology facilitates learning, it also has inherent constraints and should not be relied upon excessively. For example, when using tools such as ChatGPT, students must learn how to formulate appropriate questions, define problems clearly, and critically evaluate AI-generated information through verification and informed academic judgment. The ability to distinguish reliable information from inaccurate or misleading content is a core learning outcome.
03
When AI-generated content is incorporated into assignments, reports, or other academic work, proper citation and transparent acknowledgment of sources are required in order to comply with academic integrity and ethical standards.
(from FCU: https://cltd.fcu.edu.tw/%E9%80%A2%E7%94%B2%E9%87%9D%E5%B0%8D%E7%94%9F%E6%88%90%E5%BC%8F-ai-%E5%B7%A5%E5%85%B7%E4%B9%8B%E6%95%99%E5%AD%B8%E5%9B%A0%E6%87%89%E6%8E%AA%E6%96%BD/)

gradeRuleDescribe.ais_meno_en:
Academic Integrity & the Ethics of Writing
Welcome to a community of writers. In this class, we treat writing as a serious intellectual endeavor built on honesty, responsibility, and respect for the work of others. Adhering to academic integrity is not just about avoiding punishment; it is fundamental to your development as a critical thinker, researcher, and ethical communicator.
 
 
Academic integrity is essential to your success in this writing course. All work you submit must be your own, produced for this class during this semester.
Definitions of Violations:
  1. Plagiarism: Presenting the words, ideas, or creative work of another as your own without proper acknowledgment. This includes copying from websites, books, peers, or AI tools.
  2. Unauthorized Collaboration: Working with others on assignments intended to be individual.
  3. Multiple Submissions: Submitting the same paper for credit in more than one course without permission.
  4. AI Misuse: Using generative AI tools to produce the core content, argument, or phrasing of an assignment without (a) explicit permission for that assignment, and (b) transparent citation as outlined in class.
Citation Requirement: We will use MLA style. You must provide in-text citations and a Works Cited page for any source you reference.
 
Guidelines for the Academic Use of AI Tools
01
Under the guidance of the course instructor and in accordance with standards of academic integrity, students are expected to use AI tools responsibly to enhance learning efficiency and effectiveness and to accomplish course objectives at each stage of study.
02
Students should develop a clear understanding of the strengths, limitations, and potential implications of AI tools. While information technology facilitates learning, it also has inherent constraints and should not be relied upon excessively. For example, when using tools such as ChatGPT, students must learn how to formulate appropriate questions, define problems clearly, and critically evaluate AI-generated information through verification and informed academic judgment. The ability to distinguish reliable information from inaccurate or misleading content is a core learning outcome.
03
When AI-generated content is incorporated into assignments, reports, or other academic work, proper citation and transparent acknowledgment of sources are required in order to comply with academic integrity and ethical standards.
(Source: 逢甲大學教學發展中心)
